title: leadership-roundtable-weekly-notes-2026-03-12
content:
Meeting: Cross-team leadership roundtable
Date: 2026-03-12 10:00-11:15 PT
Attendees: Avery Chen (chair), Ravi Kumar (serving-runtime), Maya Thompson (private-deployments), Diego Alvarez (observability), Hannah Li (sre), Omar Rahman (devx), plus notes from product-hosted-api via Kate Morgan
Absentees: none noted

Agenda (pre-read sent):
- Quick wins / fire drills (10m)
- Major cross-team blockers and escalations (20m)
- Release rollouts: dedicated capacity changes & Canary plan (15m)
- Infra cost & capacity planning for Q2 (15m)
- Observability and rollback automation (10m)
- Hiring and on-call rotation adjustments (5m)
- AOB (5m)

Summary notes:
1) Quick wins / fire drills
- Serving-runtime: Ravi reported a small regression on streaming for models > 8k context; hotfix deployed to canary nodes (PR #2894). Canary metrics show 12% throughput drop on long-context paths; rolling mitigation in progress.
- Observability: Diego confirmed trace sampling adjustments pushed to reduce storage costs; sampling config rolled out to non-prod yesterday.
- SRE: Hannah called out a redis failover incident on 2026-03-11 (short outage ~4m). Root cause: delayed failover due to stale monitoring alerts; postmortem draft linked. Action assigned to Hannah.

2) Cross-team blockers and escalations
- Private deployments: Maya flagged two customers with air-gapped installs failing fingerprint checks after the last build. Investigation shows packaging checksum mismatch on package-builder image. Priority: P1 for customer impact. Owner: Maya + Diego. ETA for patch: EOD 2026-03-13.
- Console & Rollouts: Product reported inconsistent rollout state when migrating routes between clusters. Suspected race in migration controller. Owner: Ravi + Omar to triage and add unit test coverage.

3) Release rollouts: Dedicated capacity changes & Canary plan
- Planned Dedicated change: new autoscale policy (burst buffer) to be enabled 2026-03-18 across a subset of customers. Rollout plan: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 24h monitoring windows. Canary cluster shows stable latency +2ms. Decision: proceed but add automatic fallback to previous policy on 5xx spike >1.5x baseline. Owner: Platform release engineering (Diego) + product (Kate).

4) Infra cost & capacity planning for Q2
- Finance sent initial capacity budget; projections indicate a 9% GPU hour increase if growth trajectory continues. Options discussed: (a) more aggressive batching and cache tuning, (b) switch low-tier customers to quantized model variants, (c) temporary spot capacity for burst windows. Action: Omar to run workload-sim with proposed batching changes by 2026-03-19.
- Redwood Optimize: proposal to introduce model-variant recommendations on the Console to nudge customers toward lower-cost configs. Product will sketch UX flow; PM assigned: Lian Park.

5) Observability and rollback automation
- Diego demoed a prototype that ties quality regressions (from eval sets) to rollout flags and can trigger automatic rollback. Prototype relies on new eval webhooks and requires an auth flow for rollbacks. Decision: prioritize auth integration next sprint. Owner: Diego.

6) Hiring, rotations, and on-call adjustments
- On-call: Hannah requested an adjustment to postmortem SLA to 48h for high-priority incidents to allow deeper RCA work without immediate fire drills. Leadership agreed to pilot 48h for one quarter; will revisit.
- Hiring: Platform engineering approved two IC hires for infra reliability and a staff-level engineer for runtime kernel selection. Recruiting note: expedite interviews for staff role; target offer by end of April. Owner: People Ops + Ravi.

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya + Diego — patch package-builder checksum flow and publish hotfix (2026-03-13)
- Ravi + Omar — triage rollout controller race and add tests (2026-03-16)
- Hannah — finish redis postmortem and recommendations doc (2026-03-15)
- Omar — run workload sim for batching configuration and share cost delta (2026-03-19)
- Diego — finish auth integration spec for auto-rollback prototype (2026-03-20)
- Lian Park (product) — draft UX for Optimize model-variant recommendations (2026-03-22)
- People Ops — schedule expedited interviews for staff runtime role (2026-04-30)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Canary throughput regression on long-context streaming could impact high-value customers. Mitigation: keep canary, add traffic shaping to reduce long-context path exposure during peak, prepare rollback images.
- Risk: checksum hotfix timeline slipping. Mitigation: allocate an extra engineer from platform-engineering for 24h support window.
- Risk: Q2 cost overrun from unexpected usage spike. Mitigation: enforce deploy guardrails: per-route cost alerts and immediate traffic caps at 2x baseline until teams confirm capacity.

Decisions recorded:
- Approve dedicated autoscale burst buffer rollout starting 2026-03-18 with fallback policy.
- Pilot 48h postmortem SLA for high-priority incidents for one quarter.
- Prioritize auth integration for rollback automation ahead of UX polish.

Open questions:
- Should we allow product teams to opt customers into quantized model variants automatically? Need legal/PS input on opt-in/out behavior. Owner: Kate Morgan to coordinate with Legal.
- Do we want a single source-of-truth metric for per-token cost across Dedicated + Hosted? Diego to propose a dashboard spec.

Attachments / useful links:
- Redis incident postmortem (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/redis-failover-2026-03-11
- Canary metrics dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/serve/canary-streaming-2026-03-12
- Runtime PR linked above: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894
- Packaging issue ticket: JIRA-4321

Next meeting: 2026-03-19 10:00 PT
Owner for next meeting notes: Ravi Kumar

Notes: keep this doc as the running log for leadership actions. If an action is completed, prefix with [DONE] and update date. For high-severity items, add Slack pings in #platform-leads.
